annotationRationale: The triangle inequality determines the admissible integer lengths. Splitting by the number of longest sides produces two exhaustive, disjoint cases whose counts are added.
sourceMethod: Followed the official split into at least two longest sides and exactly one longest side. Made triangle feasibility, endpoint counts, and the absence of duplicates explicit.

review.mathCheck: Repeated longest sides give (2025, 2025, k), with 1 ≤ k ≤ 2025: 2025 valid triangles. A unique longest side gives (k, k, 2025), requiring 1013 ≤ k ≤ 2024: 1012 triangles. These disjoint cases include the equilateral triangle once and total 3037, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA Problem 3, page 3. It preserves the official two-case count and explicitly explains strict triangle inequalities, inclusive endpoints and nonoverlap.
review.annotationCheck: All three assessed nodes are directly exercised: triangle feasibility, integer inequality solutions and addition of disjoint counts. No material omission.
